rationale:
The subject `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.outline_source.fn` is only a signature declaration. It says `Sources::parse(&self, path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<OutlineContent, SourceError>` is an async method that outlines one file snapshot. It has no MUST clauses on behavior. Parsing behavior, inputs and error handling belong to the sibling `outline_source.behavior` and `outline_source.inputs` requirements, which this task does not judge.

The signature is exercised directly by two tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs`:
- `empty_sources_errors_and_retained_snapshots_remain_distinct` awaits `sources.parse(&file("note.txt"))` and unwraps the `Ok` value. It checks `id().path` and `id().selector`, and it shows that `text()` still returns the original snapshot after the file changes on disk. Because `parse` takes a path argument and returns an `OutlineContent` snapshot, this confirms the "outline one file snapshot" contract.
- `built_in_languages_and_structural_search_use_the_project_scope` awaits `sources.parse` for `note.unknown` and `visible.rs`. It asserts the fingerprint scheme and the outline item count.

The test `source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs` dispatches `outline_source` through the session tools. It is a marked test, and it also checks that outline dispatch registers no dependencies.

The signature obligations are covered. The `&self` receiver, the async call, the path argument, and the `Ok(OutlineContent)` result are all used and asserted on at compile time and at run time. I found no gap.
